statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6476 (PostgreSQL pg_createsubscriber allows SQL injection via subscription name) in 17.10 on the PostgreSQL 17 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6476/ lists 17.10 as the fixed release for major version 17; the advisory says versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected and 17 minor versions before 17.10 are affected, and the 17.10 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.10/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/d7de7fa84d2492f15747163cbb2f4c5c110ec4a4 on the REL_17_STABLE branch, which changes only src/bin/pg_basebackup/pg_createsubscriber.c: drop_existing_subscriptions() now escapes the subscription name with PQescapeIdentifier() before using it in the ALTER SUBSCRIPTION and DROP SUBSCRIPTION commands, and frees it with PQfreemem(); it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-6476 and is in the REL_17_10 release tag and not in REL_17_9. pg_createsubscriber ships in the postgresql17 package as /usr/libexec/postgresql17/pg_createsubscriber. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; the 17.10-r0 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/2949d6752d74a3fb36bd772b9f993331fa6917e2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, differs from the 17.9-r0 one only in the version, the tarball checksum and the secfixes list, applies no patch that touches the files this fix changes, and lists CVE-2026-6476 under its 17.10-r0 secfixes. We checked pg_createsubscriber, with the server binary's version string for each build, in every postgresql17 build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI package repository as of 2026-11-27 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, with package checksums verified against the package index: 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0 and 17.9-r0 report PostgreSQL 17.7, 17.8 and 17.9 and are affected, while 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0 report 17.10, 17.11 and 17.12 and carry the fix. The fix adds no message string, so as a check we disassembled pg_createsubscriber in every build and counted its calls into libpq: on both architectures it calls PQescapeIdentifier() 5 times and PQfreemem() 14 times in 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0 and 17.9-r0, and 6 and 15 times in 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0, matching the one added call to each in the fix (the source file has 5 and 14 such calls at REL_17_9 and 6 and 15 at REL_17_10), while its PQexec() call count, our control, is 19 in every build. 17.10-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

CVE-2026-6476 (PostgreSQL pg_createsubscriber allows SQL injection via subscription name) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 18.4: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6476/ lists 18.4 as the fixed release for major version 18. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/c2e44c370edc003367e94bde137c6d9cfab5919c ('pg_createsubscriber: Obstruct SQL injection via subscription names') on the REL_18_STABLE branch. Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-6476 under its 18.4-r0 secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with that APKBUILD from the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version. We checked every postgresql18 build published for Alpine 3.23 as of 2026-11-27 (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64. In each, the postgres server reports the PostgreSQL release matching the package version. The fix adds no message string, so we disassembled /usr/libexec/postgresql18/pg_createsubscriber (postgresql18 package) and counted call instructions to its libpq imports: the commit adds one PQescapeIdentifier and one PQfreemem call in drop_existing_subscriptions, and the counts go from 5 and 14 in 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0 and 18.3-r0 to 6 and 15 in 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0, while PQexec stays at 21 in every build. 18.4-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 carrying the fix; 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0 and 18.3-r0 are affected.
